'''''Festuca rubra''''' is a [[species]] of [[Poaceae|grass]] known by the common name '''red fescue''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''creeping red fescue''' or the '''rush-leaf fescue'''. It is widespread across much of the [[Northern Hemisphere]] and can tolerate many habitats and climates. It is best adapted to well-drained soils in cool, [[Temperate climate|temperate climates]]; it prefers shadier areas and is often planted for its shade tolerance.<ref name=usda>{{cite web |title=Plant Fact Sheet – Creeping Red Fescue |publisher=[[United States Department of Agriculture]] |url=https://plants.usda.gov/factsheet/pdf/fs_ferua3.pdf |access-date=2012-01-16}}</ref><ref name=davis>{{cite web | title = Healthy Lawns – Red Fescue  | publisher = [[University of California]] | url = http://www.ipm.ucdavis.edu/TOOLS/TURF/TURFSPECIES/redfes.html | access-date =2012-01-16 }}</ref> Wild animals browse it, but it has not been important for domestic forage due to low productivity and palatability.<ref name=usda/> It is also an [[ornamental plant]] for gardens. It functions well as a hyperaccumulator plant as well, specifically accumulating arsenic in mine affected soils.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Dradrach |first=Agnieszka |last2=Karczewska |first2=Anna |last3=Szopka |first3=Katarzyna |date=June 2020 |title=Arsenic accumulation by red fescue (Festuca rubra) growing in mine affected soils - Findings from the field and greenhouse studies |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0045653520302381 |journal=Chemosphere |language=en |volume=248 |article-number=126045 |doi=10.1016/j.chemosphere.2020.126045|doi-access=free }}</ref>

==Description==
''Festuca rubra'' is [[perennial]] and has sub-species that have [[rhizome]]s and/or form [[bunchgrass]] tufts. It mainly exists in neutral and acidic soils. It can grow between 2 and 20 cm tall.

Like all fescues, the leaves are narrow and needle like, making it less palatable to [[livestock]]. The swards that it forms are not as tufted as [[sheep's fescue]] (''Festuca ovina'') or wavy hair grass (''[[Deschampsia flexuosa]]'').  The tufted nature is what gives the grass its springy characteristic.  The leaves are bright green.

=== Flowers ===

There are 4 to 10 [[spikelet]] flowers, which are up to 15 mm long.

The [[ligule]] is very short and blunt.<ref name=BSBI>{{cite web |url=http://www.bsbi.org.uk/TEP_Festuca_rubra.pdf |publisher=[[Botanical Society of Britain and Ireland|BSBI]] |title=Festuca rubra – Red fescue |access-date=2010-11-16}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
''Festuca rubra'', as red fescue or creeping red fescue, is cultivated as an ornamental plant for use as a [[Lawn|turfgrass]] and [[groundcover]]. It can be left completely unmowed, or occasionally trimmed for a lush [[meadow]]-like look. There are many subspecies, and many [[cultivar]]s have been bred for the [[horticulture]] trade.
